Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Build `linkvault`, a small URL-shortener HTTP JSON API with a command-line client, in the `linkvault/` package at the root of this workspace. Use only the Python 3.11+ standard library: `http.server` for the server and `sqlite3` for storage; pytest is allowed for your own tests. An admin key issues bearer tokens, and each token can create, list, inspect and delete only its own short links. Short links redirect with HTTP 302, can carry an optional custom slug and expiry, and count their clicks. Each token is rate-limited, and all data except rate-limit counters survives a server restart. The server binds 127.0.0.1 only, prints one ready line, supports a fake clock for testing, and shuts down cleanly on Ctrl+C on Windows, macOS and Linux. Follow `contract.md` exactly, because an automated test suite checks status codes, JSON keys and key order, headers, output and exit codes. Keep the code minimal and readable, and include tests for the behaviour you build.
# linkvault: Interface Contract

## Constraints

- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, stdlib only (`http.server`, `sqlite3`, `json`, `argparse`, `urllib`, `secrets`, `hashlib`, `threading`, `signal`); pytest for tests only.
- **Package location:** `linkvault/` at the workspace root (`linkvault/__init__.py`, `linkvault/__main__.py`); commands run with the workspace root as cwd.
- **Entry points:** `python -m linkvault serve ...` (server); `python -m linkvault <client-cmd> ...` (client).

## Functional requirements

- **R1 Server start.** `serve` opens or creates the DB, binds 127.0.0.1, then prints exactly one ready line to stdout. Nothing else is ever written to stdout; logs go to stderr.
- **R2 Token issuance.** `POST /v1/tokens` with the correct admin key returns a new token. The token is `lv_` followed by 32 lowercase hex characters (`secrets.token_hex(16)`). Only its SHA-256 hex digest is stored.
- **R3 Authentication.** Every `/v1/links` route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A missing, malformed or unknown token returns 401.
- **R4 Create link.** `POST /v1/links` stores `url` with a custom `slug` or a generated slug, and an optional `expires_in`.
- **R5 Slug rules.** Slugs are case-sensitive. A custom slug must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` and must not be `healthz`. A generated slug is 7 characters from `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789`, drawn with `secrets.choice`. It is regenerated if it already exists or is reserved, with up to 5 attempts and then 500. Creating an existing slug returns 409.
- **R6 URL rules.** The scheme is `http` or `https` (case-insensitive). `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname` is non-empty. The URL is at most 2048 characters and contains no whitespace or control characters (code points < 0x21 or 0x7F). It is stored and redirected to verbatim.
- **R7 Resolve.** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with `Location: <url>` and an empty body. It atomically increments `clicks` and sets `last_clicked_at` to now.
- **R8 Missing and expired links.** An unknown slug returns 404. A link with `now >= expires_at` returns 410 and its click count is unchanged. Comparisons use whole seconds.
- **R9 List and inspect.** A token can list its own links (expired ones included) and fetch one link with its stats. Another token's link always returns 404, never 403.
- **R10 Delete.** A token can delete its own link. Afterwards the slug resolves 404 and is free to reuse.
- **R11 Rate limit.** Requests are counted per token in fixed 60-second windows aligned to the Unix epoch (`window_start = now - now % 60`). The limit is `--rate-limit` (default 60) counted requests per window. A request is counted when it reaches the rate-limit step (see precedence in Error handling), whatever its final status. Request number `limit + 1` and later in the same window return 429 with `Retry-After: <window_start + 60 - now>`. Counters are in memory and reset on restart. Redirects, `/healthz` and admin routes are not rate-limited.
- **R12 Clock.** "Now" is integer Unix seconds (floor of real time). With `--fake-clock <ISO>`, now is frozen at that instant and changes only through `POST /v1/admin/clock`. The fake clock is not persisted.
- **R13 Persistence.** Tokens, links, clicks and `last_clicked_at` survive a restart on the same `--db`.
- **R14 Concurrency.** The server is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`. N concurrent redirects to one slug leave `clicks == N` exactly.
- **R15 Shutdown.** On SIGINT, SIGTERM (POSIX) or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT/SIGBREAK (Windows), the server stops accepting connections, closes the DB and exits 0 within 5 seconds.
- **R16 Client.** CLI commands wrap the API. Each prints the response body to stdout, and uses the exit codes below.

## Interface contract

### Conventions

- Timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC with whole seconds. They are stored as INTEGER Unix seconds.
- JSON responses are encoded with `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` in UTF-8, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every response sets `Content-Length`; a 204 response has an empty body and MUST send `Content-Length: 0`. Keys appear in exactly the order listed below.
- Request `Content-Type` is ignored. The body is read using `Content-Length` (absent means empty), and the maximum is 8192 bytes.
- Query strings are ignored on every route. Paths are matched exactly, with no trailing-slash normalisation. Any (method, path) pair not listed below returns 404 `not_found`.
- `short_url` is `http://127.0.0.1:<bound port>/<slug>`.

**Link object** (key order is fixed): `{"slug", "url", "short_url", "created_at", "expires_at", "clicks", "last_clicked_at"}`. `expires_at` and `last_clicked_at` are `null` until they are set.

### Server CLI

```
python -m linkvault serve --db PATH --admin-key KEY [--port N] [--rate-limit N] [--fake-clock ISO]
```

| Flag | Rule |
|---|---|
| `--db` | Required. The file is created if missing, and its parent directory must exist. |
| `--admin-key` | Required. Non-empty string. |
| `--port` | 0-65535, default 8000. The value 0 binds an OS-chosen free port. |
| `--rate-limit` | Integer >= 1, default 60. |
| `--fake-clock` | An ISO timestamp in the format above. It enables the admin clock route. |

Ready line: `LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by a line terminator, which may be `\n` or `\r\n`. It uses the actual bound port, is flushed immediately, and nothing else is written to stdout before it.

Exit codes: 0 for a clean shutdown; 2 for a usage error (argparse); 3 if the port cannot be bound or the DB cannot be opened, with a message to stderr.

### Endpoints

| # | Method and path | Auth | Request body | Success response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | `GET /healthz` | none | none | 200 `{"status":"ok"}` |
| E2 | `POST /v1/tokens` | `X-Admin-Key: <key>` | ignored | 201 `{"token":"lv_…","created_at":"…"}` |
| E3 | `POST /v1/links` | Bearer | `{"url": str, "slug"?: str, "expires_in"?: int}` | 201, link object |
| E4 | `GET /v1/links` | Bearer | none | 200 `{"links":[link…]}` ordered by `created_at` ascending, then `slug` ascending |
| E5 | `GET /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 200, link object |
| E6 | `DELETE /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 204, empty body |
| E7 | `GET /<slug>` | none | none | 302, `Location: <url>`, `Content-Length: 0`, empty body |
| E8 | `POST /v1/admin/clock` | `X-Admin-Key` | `{"now": ISO}` | 200 `{"now":"…"}`. The route exists only with `--fake-clock`; otherwise it returns 404. Any valid timestamp is accepted. |

E3 body rules:
- The body is a JSON object with no extra keys.
- `url` is required and must follow R6.
- `slug` is optional and must follow R5. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400).
- `expires_in` is optional. It is an integer from 1 to 31536000, and `bool` values are rejected. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400). It sets `expires_at = created_at + expires_in`.

E8 body rules:
- The body must be exactly `{"now": ISO}`, where ISO is a string in the timestamp format above.
- A missing `now` key, an extra key, a wrong type or an unparseable timestamp returns 400 `invalid_request`.

A wrong or missing admin key on E2 or E8 returns 401. On E5, E6 and E7, a `<slug>` that fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` is a route mismatch, so it returns 404 at the route step, before auth.

### DB schema (exact)

```sql
PRAGMA user_version = 1;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  url TEXT NOT NULL,
  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tokens(token_hash),
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER,
  clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_clicked_at INTEGER);
```

A click is recorded with one statement: `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?`.

### Client CLI

The server URL comes from `--server URL`, or else the `LINKVAULT_SERVER` environment variable. The token comes from `--token T`, or else `LINKVAULT_TOKEN`. Both options are accepted after the subcommand.

| Command | Calls | Stdout on success |
|---|---|---|
| `token create --admin-key K` | E2 | Response JSON, one line |
| `shorten URL [--slug S] [--expires-in N]` | E3 | Response JSON, one line |
| `list` | E4 | Response JSON, one line |
| `stats SLUG` | E5 | Response JSON, one line |
| `delete SLUG` | E6 | Nothing |

Output is re-serialised with the server's `json.dumps` settings and ends with `\n`. Client exit codes:

| Code | Meaning | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2xx response | as above |
| 1 | non-2xx response | Error JSON on stderr, stdout empty |
| 2 | usage error, or a missing server or token | Message on stderr |
| 3 | connection failure | Message on stderr |

## Error handling

Every error body has this shape: `{"error":{"code":"<code>","message":"<text>"}}`. Tests assert `code` only.

| Condition | Status | code |
|---|---|---|
| No route matches the method and path; unknown or foreign slug | 404 | `not_found` |
| Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token; bad admin key | 401 | `unauthorized` |
| Over the rate limit (adds a `Retry-After` header) | 429 | `rate_limited` |
| `Content-Length` > 8192 (the response sets `Connection: close` and the body is not read) | 413 | `payload_too_large` |
| Body is not valid UTF-8 JSON, or is not an object | 400 | `invalid_json` |
| Schema violation: missing or extra key, wrong type, bad URL, slug, `expires_in` or `now` | 400 | `invalid_request` |
| Slug already exists, or is reserved (`healthz`) | 409 | `slug_taken` |
| Link expired (E7 only) | 410 | `gone` |
| Unhandled exception | 500 | `internal` |

Precedence (first failure wins): route 404 → auth 401 → rate limit 429 → size 413 → JSON 400 → validation 400 → resource state 404/409/410.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (R1, R15):** `serve --port 0` prints exactly the `LISTENING` line. `GET /healthz` returns 200. SIGINT (or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows) makes it exit 0 within 5 s.
- **AC2 (R2):** E2 with the right key returns 201 and a token matching `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`. With a wrong key it returns 401. The DB holds the SHA-256 of the token, never the plaintext.
- **AC3 (R3):** E3, E4 and E5 without a valid bearer token return 401 `unauthorized`.
- **AC4 (R4, R5):** E3 without `slug` returns a slug matching `^[a-z0-9]{7}$`. A custom `slug` is echoed back. A repeated slug returns 409. `healthz` and `ab` return 409 and 400 respectively.
- **AC5 (R6):** `ftp://x`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `http://`, a URL with a space, and a 2049-character URL each return 400 `invalid_request`.
- **AC6 (R7):** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with the exact `Location`. A later E5 shows `clicks` 1 and `last_clicked_at` set to now.
- **AC7 (R8, R12):** With the fake clock at T and `expires_in=60`, the link resolves 302 at T+59 and 410 at T+60. Its clicks stay at the T+59 value.
- **AC8 (R9, R10):** Token B gets 404 on E5 and E6 for token A's slug. A's E4 lists only A's links in order. After E6, `GET /<slug>` returns 404 and the slug can be created again.
- **AC9 (R11):** With `--rate-limit 3` and the fake clock at a window start plus 10 s, requests 1-3 succeed. Request 4 returns 429 with `Retry-After: 50`. After the clock moves to the next window, the next request succeeds. Redirects are never limited.
- **AC10 (R13):** After a restart on the same DB, tokens still authenticate, and links and clicks are unchanged.
- **AC11 (R14):** 50 concurrent `GET /<slug>` requests leave `clicks == 50`.
- **AC12 (R16):** `shorten` prints the link JSON and exits 0. A 409 makes it exit 1 with empty stdout. An unreachable server makes it exit 3. A missing token makes it exit 2.

# linkvault technology research: report

I checked the behaviour below by running small local experiments on Python 3.9.6 (the macOS `agent-py` interpreter) and wrote no files in the workspace. The only other interpreter on this machine is 3.14, so nothing was run on 3.11. The doc links are the canonical official pages. I did not re-fetch them, so the doc-based claims come from my knowledge of them, not from a fresh read. The one exception is Windows behaviour, which I could not run here and mark "(docs)".

## Key findings

**1. Shutdown**
1. Calling `server.shutdown()` from a signal handler deadlocks when `serve_forever` runs in the main thread. The handler runs in the main thread, and `shutdown()` waits for `serve_forever` to exit. I reproduced this: with SIGINT and SIGTERM the process was still alive after 5 s and had to be killed.
2. The pattern that works is `serve_forever(poll_interval=0.1)` in the main thread. The handler starts `threading.Thread(target=server.shutdown, daemon=True).start()`. After `serve_forever` returns, call `server_close()`, then close the DB, then exit 0. I tested this with an idle keep-alive connection still open: SIGINT and SIGTERM both gave exit code 0 in about 0.13 s.
3. `ThreadingHTTPServer` sets `daemon_threads = True`. Handler threads are therefore not joined, even though `block_on_close` is `True`, so idle keep-alive connections cannot hold up exit. Do not set `daemon_threads = False`.
4. `signal.signal` only works in the main thread. Install handlers for `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM`, plus `signal.SIGBREAK` where it exists (use `getattr(signal, "SIGBREAK", None)`).
5. Windows (docs): `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` arrives as `SIGBREAK`, and Python installs no default handler for it, so the process would simply die with a non-zero code. The test harness must start the child with `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` and send `os.kill(pid, signal.CTRL_BREAK_EVENT)`. `CTRL_C_EVENT` arrives as `SIGINT`. Python-level handlers only run after `select` returns, so latency is at most `poll_interval`.
6. Windows (docs): SIGTERM is never delivered by the OS. It is harmless to register.
7. Windows (docs and known issue, not tested): `HTTPServer.allow_reuse_address = 1` sets `SO_REUSEADDR`, which on Windows lets a second socket bind a port already in use. That would defeat the exit-3 bind-failure check. Set `allow_reuse_address = False` on Windows (`sys.platform == "win32"`). Port 0 makes this moot in most tests.
8. A bind failure raises `OSError` from the `ThreadingHTTPServer(...)` constructor. Catch it, write a message to stderr and exit 3. The bound port is `server.server_address[1]`, which I confirmed with port 0 and `("127.0.0.1", 0)`, giving `AF_INET`.

**2. BaseHTTPRequestHandler**
9. The default `protocol_version` is `"HTTP/1.0"`, which closes the connection after every response. With `"HTTP/1.1"`, keep-alive is on. Every response then needs `Content-Length`, including 204 and 302, and any response that leaves a request body unread must set `Connection: close` and `self.close_connection = True`. Otherwise the leftover bytes are parsed as the next request. The contract requires `Content-Length` everywhere, so either version works. HTTP/1.0 is the simplest and safest choice. If you use 1.1, the shutdown behaviour in findings 2 and 3 still holds.
10. `log_message(self, fmt, *args)` is the hook. Override it to write to `sys.stderr`, or to do nothing. The default already writes to stderr, but the override makes it explicit. `log_error` calls `log_message`. Nothing in `http.server` writes to stdout.
11. A 204 with `Content-Length: 0` works with `send_response(204)`, `send_header("Content-Length", "0")` and `end_headers()`, and no body write. I confirmed the output is `HTTP/1.1 204 No Content ... Content-Length: 0`. `send_response` adds `Server` and `Date` headers automatically, which is fine.
12. `http.server` returns `501 Unsupported method` for any method without a `do_X`. I confirmed this for PUT and HEAD. To meet "any unlisted method/path pair returns 404 `not_found`", define `do_GET`, `do_POST`, `do_DELETE`, `do_PUT`, `do_PATCH`, `do_HEAD` and `do_OPTIONS` (all routed through one dispatcher). A HEAD reply must have no body but may keep `Content-Length`. Other verbs (TRACE, CONNECT and the like) still get 501, and `send_error` emits an HTML body. Override `send_error` to emit JSON if you want full coverage; this is optional.
13. For 413: send the response with `Connection: close` and do not read the body. A 9000-byte body arrived and the 413 was received cleanly. With 200 KB and 5 MB bodies, the client's `send` hit `BrokenPipeError` mid-upload, though on loopback macOS the 413 was still readable afterwards. On Linux, closing a socket with unread data can send RST and discard the response in the client's buffer. The contract forbids reading the body, so tests should send small oversize bodies (for example 8193 to 20000 bytes). Optionally, drain a bounded amount (for example up to 64 KB) after sending the response; this is not required by the contract.
14. `Content-Length` parsing: absent means empty. A non-numeric or negative value is unspecified by the contract. I recommend answering 400 `invalid_request` with `Connection: close`. A negative value passed to `rfile.read` would block.
15. Path handling: `self.path` is the raw request target. Strip the query with `self.path.split("?", 1)[0]`. Do not use `urlsplit(self.path).path`, because a target starting with `//x/y` is parsed as a netloc, giving `/y` (I confirmed this). Do not percent-decode, since the contract says paths are matched exactly.
16. Slug regex: the contract writes `^...$`. With `re.match`, `$` also matches before a trailing newline, so `"abc\n"` matched. Use `re.fullmatch` on the bare pattern (`fullmatch` returned False). Likewise, `\d` matches Unicode digits, so use `[0-9]`.
17. URL validation: `urlsplit(url)` can raise `ValueError` (for example `http://[bad` gives "Invalid IPv6 URL"), so wrap it and return 400. For `http://`, `.hostname` is `None` (confirmed). `urlsplit` lowercases the scheme, so `HTTP://x` passes as required. Check control characters and whitespace with `any(ord(c) < 0x21 or ord(c) == 0x7f for c in url)`. Check the length with `len(url) <= 2048`. Unicode characters above 0x7F are allowed by the rules as written; the response JSON uses `ensure_ascii=True`, but the `Location` header must be latin-1 encodable. A non-ASCII URL would make `send_header` raise `UnicodeEncodeError` and produce a 500, so decide whether to reject it or encode it. Verbatim redirect plus the stated rules leaves this undefined; flag it in the spec.

**3. sqlite3**
18. Use one connection with `check_same_thread=False` and one global `threading.Lock` around every DB operation. This is simpler than per-thread connections and gives exact `clicks == N`. `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?` is atomic inside SQLite on its own. The lock mainly protects the shared connection, and the select-then-update sequence for 302 versus 410 versus 404.
19. Use `isolation_level=None` (autocommit). Each statement then commits itself, no `commit()` calls are needed, and `in_transaction` is False. This behaves the same on 3.9 and 3.11. Do not use the `autocommit=` attribute, which is 3.12+. The default `isolation_level=""` opens an implicit transaction before DML, and you must commit every write.
20. Schema: `conn.executescript("PRAGMA user_version = 1; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ...")` works, and the version reads back as `(1,)`. Run it on every start; it is idempotent. `REFERENCES tokens` is not enforced unless `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, so leave it off (the delete flow is unaffected).
21. Persistence: the default rollback journal (`DELETE` mode) is durable across restart once a statement commits. WAL is unnecessary and leaves `-wal` and `-shm` side files that complicate tests which copy or compare the DB. Keep the default.
22. A missing parent directory raises `sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file` at `connect()` (confirmed). A directory given as the path gives the same error. A file that is not a database raises `sqlite3.DatabaseError: file is not a database` at the first statement (confirmed), which is the `executescript`, not at `connect`. Wrap connect and schema setup together in `except sqlite3.Error` (or `(sqlite3.Error, OSError)`) and exit 3 with a stderr message. Do this before binding the socket, or close the socket on failure.
23. Shutdown order: `server.shutdown()`, then `server.server_close()`, then take the DB lock, then `conn.close()`. Handler threads are daemon threads and may still be mid-request, so the lock avoids closing during a query.

**4. Ready line and logging**
24. Use `print(f"LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:{port}", flush=True)`, which works when stdout is a pipe. `sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)` also exists (3.7+) but is not needed. On Windows, text-mode stdout writes `\r\n`, which the contract allows. Print the line only after the DB is open and the socket is bound, and before `serve_forever`.
25. Keep all logging on stderr. Argparse errors already go to stderr and exit 2. Make sure no `print()` appears elsewhere in the server path. Traceback output for unhandled exceptions should go to stderr (`traceback.print_exc()` goes to stderr by default).

**5. Python 3.9 versus 3.11 traps**
26. `datetime.fromisoformat("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z")` raises `ValueError` on 3.9 (confirmed) but works on 3.11. Do not use it.
27. `datetime.strptime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")` is too lenient, as it accepted `"2026-1-1T0:0:0Z"` (confirmed). Use `re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z", s)` first. Then build `datetime.datetime(y, mo, d, h, mi, s)`, which raises `ValueError` for Feb 30, hour 24 and second 60. Then take `calendar.timegm(dt.timetuple())`.
28. To format: `time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(n))`, or `datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(n, datetime.timezone.utc)` with `strftime`. Avoid `datetime.UTC`, which is 3.11 only.
29. Syntax and typing: add `from __future__ import annotations` to every module if you write `X | None` annotations. A runtime `X | Y` (in `isinstance` or an alias) fails on 3.9. Avoid `match` statements, parenthesised context managers, `zip(strict=True)`, `typing.Self`, `StrEnum`, `tomllib`, `ExceptionGroup` and `asyncio.TaskGroup`.
30. Python 3.11+ patched `http.server` so that a request target starting with `//` is collapsed (gh-87389). Behaviour for `//x` therefore differs between 3.9 and 3.11+. Expect 404 either way.
31. Do not use `sqlite3.Connection.autocommit` or `PRAGMA` features newer than SQLite 3.31.

## Constraints the spec must respect
- Never call `server.shutdown()` directly in the signal handler. It must run in a separate thread, with `serve_forever` in the main thread.
- Handlers must be installed in the main thread, including `SIGBREAK` on Windows when present.
- Define `do_*` methods for HEAD, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, POST and GET at least, so unlisted pairs get 404 `not_found` and not 501.
- Every response sets `Content-Length`, with `0` for 204 and 302. 413 and any unread-body path set `Connection: close`.
- Match slugs with `re.fullmatch` and an ASCII-only class. Wrap `urlsplit` in `try/except ValueError`.
- A DB or bind failure exits 3 with a stderr message, and nothing is printed to stdout before the ready line.
- No 3.11-only APIs, so the code also runs on 3.9.
- Do not read the body on 413.

## Recommendations
- Use `protocol_version = "HTTP/1.0"` by default. Switch to "HTTP/1.1" only if a keep-alive test is expected, and then also close the connection on 413 and on bad `Content-Length`.
- One connection, `isolation_level=None`, one `threading.Lock`, a single `executescript` for the schema, no WAL.
- Handler-side flow: dispatch to one `_route` function, build the response through one `_send_json(status, obj, headers)` helper, and wrap everything in `try/except Exception` that returns 500 `internal`.
- Add a spec line for non-ASCII URLs, since `Location` must be latin-1 encodable. Either reject the URL as 400 or percent-encode only the header.
- Add a spec line for an invalid `Content-Length` (400 `invalid_request`, close the connection).
- For the Windows bind check: set `allow_reuse_address = False` on win32.
- Tests: spawn `serve --port 0` as a subprocess, read the ready line, open a keep-alive connection, send SIGINT, and assert exit 0 within 5 s. Skip the Windows variant unless running on Windows.
